data.name: Zaccai
data.gender_notes: Zaccai is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Hebrew 'zakah' meaning 'to remember' or 'remembered'. In the Bible, Zacchaeus was a tax collector who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus and repented, returning fourfold what he had stolen. The name Zaccai carries the meaning “God remembered” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zaccai usually hope their child will grow to embody god remembered and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of repentance and dedication to God.
data.etymology: Zaccai belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God remembered.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zaccai total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: צַכָּאי
in_hebrew.meaning: פרי פירות, ילד, נצח, רב, דביר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: צַכָּאי הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'פרי פירות' או 'ילד'. במקרא, 'צַכָּא' נזכר כשם אדם, ובספר ישעיה, הוא נזכר כאחד מן ה'מלכי ישראל הגדולים'. במסורת יהודית, 'צַכָּא' הוא שם של דמות מקראית, ובספר היובלים, הוא נזכר כאחד מן 'כנעני הדביר'. בזיקה לכנעני, שם 'צַכָּא' נזכר כ'בן דביר', ובאחד הפסוקים, הוא נזכר כ'אדם'.

in_greek.name: Ζακαῖος
in_greek.long_meaning: ὁ Ζακαῖος (ὁ Ζακαῖος) είναι ονομασία που προέρχεται από το ἁκαῖος, που σημαίνει 'παραγωγός' ή 'γεννητής'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ὁ Ζακαῖος είναι το όνομα του πατέρα του Ιωάννη του Ευαγγελιστή, και κατά την παράδοση, ο Ζακαῖος ήταν ο προφήτης που μαντεύτηκε την γέννηση του Ιωάννη, και έδωσε στο παιδί του το όνομα 'Ιωάννης'.

in_latin.name: Zacchaeus
in_latin.long_meaning: Zacchaeus est nomen Hebraicum quod significat 'producentis' aut 'natoris'. In Novo Testamento, Zacchaeus est nomen patris Ioannis Evangelistae, et secundum traditio, Zacchaeus fuit propheta qui praedixit nativitatem Ioannis, et dedit filio suo nomen 'Ioannes'.

in_english.name: Zaccai
in_english.meaning: fruit of the vine, child, eternal, great
in_english.long_meaning: Zaccai is a Hebrew name meaning 'fruit of the vine' or 'child'. In the Bible, Zaccai is mentioned as a name of a man, and in the book of Isaiah, he is mentioned as one of the 'kings of Israel'. In Jewish tradition, Zaccai is the name of a biblical figure, and in the book of Jubbim, he is mentioned as one of the 'Canaanites of Debir'. Linked to the Canaanite, the name Zaccai is mentioned as 'son of Debir', and in one of the verses, he is mentioned as 'man'.

data.cultural_impact: Zacchaeus is often remembered in Christian history as the short man who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus in the Gospel of Luke (Luke 19:1-10). This story has been depicted in various artworks and religious texts, highlighting the importance of intent and determination in seeking spiritual growth. Zaccai, as a named derived from this biblical figure, carries a rich history of perseverance and the pursuit of personal betterment.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zaccai holds significant spiritual meaning from the biblical story of Zacchaeus. His repentance and subsequent humility were demonstrated through his offer to give back fourfold what he had stolen, symbolizing a complete transformation and a commitment to restore harmony and balance. As a Christian name, Zaccai serves as a reminder of the power of repentance and the importance of seeking spiritual growth, even through seemingly insurmountable obstacles. This name calls to mind the idea that no sin is too great for God's forgiveness and the possibility of redemption.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zaccai (or Zacchaeus): A man of short stature, filled with curiosity and longing for God, climbed a sycamore tree to catch a glimpse of Jesus. In doing so, he not only regained physical sight, but also gained spiritual vision, repenting and offering half of his possessions to the poor. This act of humility and contrition symbolizes the transformative power of faith.

biblical_reference.note: Zaccai is mentioned as a name of a man in the book of Isaiah.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Zacchaeus' is mentioned in the New Testament of the Bible in the book of Luke (19:1-10). He was a chief tax collector in Jericho, and was a wealthy man.
historical_references.context: The New Testament narrative describes Zacchaeus as a short man who wanted to see Jesus when He passed through Jericho. He climbed a sycamore tree to get a better view, and Jesus called out to him and invited Himself to Zacchaeus' house. After this encounter, Zacchaeus was moved by his encounter with Jesus and promised to give half of his wealth to the poor and to make restitution for any extortions he had committed.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Zacchaeus can be found in the Talmud, a collection of Jewish texts, in which he is mentioned as a descendant of Eliezer ben Hyrcanus, a prominent Tanna (rabbinic sage) in the late 1st and early 2nd centuries AD. This shows that, while Zacchaeus' actions as a tax collector were not in line with Jewish law, he was still considered to be part of the Jewish community.
historical_references.context: The Talmudic reference to Zacchaeus as a descendant of Eliezer ben Hyrcanus indicates that he was a Jewish tax collector working for the Roman government, as Eliezer ben Hyrcanus was a contemporary of Herod the Great. This reference also suggests that Zacchaeus may have had some level of support or acceptance within the Jewish community despite his role as a tax collector.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Zaccai is of Hebrew origin and translates to 'pure'. In modern times, this name has gained popularity in various contexts, particularly in business ethics, philanthropy, and spiritual awakening. On professional networking sites like LinkedIn, individuals named Zaccai might be seen as role models for their ethical business practices, inspiring others to follow suit. On social media platforms like Facebook and Twitter, Zaccai is often used in discussions about philanthropy and charity work, as well as in spiritual contexts related to personal growth and enlightenment.
